subject: Renewal: aligning term + ramped capacity with credit bands
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@clearpath.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearpath.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion + request to align term

Hi Olga,

We're preparing for our renewal and want to propose a slightly different structure than what we've done historically. Clearpath is looking to move to a 2-year committed term, but we have a strong seasonality profile and would prefer a ramped delivery of committed capacity: approximately 40% in year 1 (starting at renewal effective date) and the remaining 60% in year 2.

A few asks from procurement/legal:
- Can Redwood co-term this amendment with our existing platform agreement so both contracts end together (we're targeting co-term date of 2029-07-31)?
- We'd like a clear credit-band approach for unused committed capacity (carryover credits up to a band) rather than automatic forfeiture.
- Procurement prefers annual invoicing tied to the committed tier; can you confirm invoicing cadence and if you can accept a PO? (we will issue PO-5789).
- Finally, we want auto-renew turned off at the amendment level so we can reevaluate prior to year 3.

Attaching a short summary of our internal expected usage for FY28 (internal). Would love a short proposal from your side on pricing bands and an updated amendment draft.

Thanks — happy to hop on 30 minutes next week.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Partnerships
Clearpath Analytics

---
Alicia's attachment: clearpath_usage_estimates_q1-q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@clearpath.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + request to align term

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file.

We can absolutely support a two-year term with a ramped commitment. To make this concrete, I've sketched a credit-band approach attached (RDW_proposed_amendment_v1.docx) that shows:
- Year 1 commit = 40% of contracted units; Year 2 commit = remaining 60%
- Credit bands: up to 10% of annual commit carries to the next year; up to 25% in exceptional carryover with applied fee; anything above forfeits.
- Invoicing: annual in arrears by default, but we can invoice annual prepay on request (would require finance approval).
- Co-term: we can co-term to 2029-07-31 as requested; legal will bake that into the amendment wording.
- Auto-renew: we'll set amendment to opt-out (no auto-renew) per your ask.

Proposed discounts for the ramped structure: 7.5% year-1 effective pricing (because of lower utilization density) with a true-up at the start of year 2 if usage materially exceeds estimate.

I've attached RDW_proposed_amendment_v1.docx for review and a rough credit band pricing table inline. If this looks directionally correct, can we schedule a 30-min sync with procurement and finance (Alicia + procurement team) Friday 15th or Monday 18th?

Thanks,
Olga
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW_proposed_amendment_v1.docx (proposed amendment + credit band sketch)
Related: https://drive.redwood.com/rdw-2091/proposal

- Requesting credit-band carryover policy instead of forfeiture (our draft allows 10% carry into next year; up to 25% with fee).
- Procurement asked for net-60 on the year-1 invoice.

Can finance confirm if net-60 one-time is acceptable to revenue ops? Also need legal to quick-turn the amendment with co-terming language and opt-out auto-renew. I'm proposing a modest commercial concession: 5% additional discount if they commit to an early true-up clause (true-up at month 3 of year 2) — keeps our unit economics intact while addressing their seasonal profile.

Please reply with: 
1) finance: accept net-60 year-1?
2) legal: confirm co-term clause timeline and any compliance flags?
3) commercial: ok to offer 5% incentive tied to early true-up?

I've attached the PO and my draft amendment; will join the meeting if you want me to.
